title: A question suddenly occurred to me
author: Amiya_desi
selftext: Right now, you can usually only identify AI-generated games by their visuals and music; as for the code, there’s really no way to know without decompiling it. But if someone uses AI to generate initial game assets—and then manually redraws and rearranges the music based on the best results from the AI's output—would that still count as an AI game?

comments.author: caxco93
comments.body: bro, just polish your game and it's good. AI is a tool. lots of professionals stopped writing code manually months ago.

replies.author: anon999387
replies.body: Even if they didn't want to, the expectation for how fast something is completed is now often measured at AI assisted levels and many have no choice.

replies.author: HurryOne
replies.body: True. My job has performance metrics based on how often we use ai. They require us to use ai to assist our codebase. It's a mess.

replies.author: adelie42
replies.body:
People seem to use AI and low effort interchangeably. Game stores have been filled with low effort slop for as long as game stores have existed. Low effort AI generated assets all look the same because "Build game assets. Make no mistakes", the little randomness has been completely exhausted.

For example, I have a terrain generator and spend quite a few hours writing out the spec, and yet another for several the shader, and once I got the initial proof of concept, it has been many hours more tweaking it to get it to look just the way I want; most notably the first round is exactly what I asked for but didn't like, which took me back to research. I think it is unique and playable, but still needs more work.

Its just a different process and I am still mildly impressed by what I see here as "one shot", but by impressed I mean, wow, what a wonderful place to start your work.

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body:
Have you heard about vegans? They don't eat meat, they don't drink milk, they don't wear leather, they don't use shampoo tested on anymals, some are strictly againt having pets.

With this in mind, there's two parts of AI art. Quality part is, AI art is very generic and boring, and human art has a big variety. Redrawing the faces and hands in your style and/or drawing after AI generated concept - this makes the final image much better. Issue solved, quality improved, no one would ever spot AI

The ethical part is, anti AI will hate it anyway. If you heavily edit AI picture, or redraw the AI concept by hand, or use it for inspiration, or if your product is 100% made manually, but anime girl on your PFP is AI generated - the digital vegans will bully you for it.

comments.author: ChirpXel
comments.body:
Well in steams terms to avoid the "Made with AI" tag, no actually. It is NOT considered AI-generated anymore.   
  
But you must make a significant amount of change from the AI generated content for it to be considered human made instead.

comments.author: Hot_Professional8287
comments.body: Yes, it would still count as an AI-assisted game, but that's where the industry needs to go. AI belongs UNDER the hood. Once people start frequently delivering polished, AI-assisted games, then the stigma is going to go away. It'll become a general quality check like anything else.

comments.author: aberroco
comments.body: It's quite possible to say when the code was AI generated by the bugs that happen. Bugs that no human would make in the first place. Not because humans write perfect code, of course we aren't, but because this kind of bugs seems intentional, impossible to make by mistake, and it's rooted from lack of understanding of how the final behavior should... well, behave.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: I don't see it.  Each new gen of AI coding tool is better and better at finding bugs.  I'd say today's generation is far better than most people

replies.author: aberroco
replies.body: That is if such bugs would be detected by humans, because they aren't bugs for AI, they're working as intended, where intention was never specified and was simply guessed by AI writing the code.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body:
Oh, that's not a bug, that's a spec gap.  

That's a planning and review mistake for the dev using the tool, not a failure of the tool itself.  Grill me and other things like that are great for ironing out specs.  But definitely user error.

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body: If it's a published game, nobody's looking at your source code anyway

comments.author: Faratas14
comments.body:
Ai is very very fast for prototyping.
You can do a vertical slice and know if it will function or not.

After that, there's a long way to publish it, if you care about it.

I've been using AI since Codex Release in cloud and it's misleading to say "it's easy to develop games with AI".

Iterating, quality control, original assets, even made with AI are good.

comments.author: Fun-Mission-6068
comments.body: Yes, it would. AI was used in the development, so it would be an AI game. What you're talking about is essentially Concept Art/Music, where a concept is made and then a final piece is made from it.

comments.author: Am_Biyori
comments.body: I'm gonna climb out on a limb here and say that, for games were all the coding is AI, you can tell if it was used by looking at the game. Doubly so if the AI was used to code UIs or partical effects. Just like with graphics, the AI has developed its own preferences for coding how things move and are displayed. Add to that the fact that, at least for now AIs, hasn't worked out a formula for 'feel'.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: It's easy to decompile code these days. Even for "more secure" engines. And for engines like Godot it's basically completely exposed with little work. For this reason I don't suggest trying to hide  your AI use when you need to disclose it. You don't need to go out of your way to tell everyone you used AI, but when something contractually requires you to do so, don't lie about it. In the long run, people won't care that you used AI in your game if it's good... They WILL care long-term if they feel like you deceived them.

replies.author: Amiya_desi
replies.body: Okay, then let's just say we used AI. Anyway, if it can't even reach this level, there's nothing more to say.：）

comments.author: SlowAsLightning
comments.body: Under steam disclosure policy, yes. This doesn't apply everywhere but for steam specifically the usage of generative ai to create "player facing" assets (essentially everything except code, game design documents, etc.) means that that game has to have an AI disclosure.
